newsitem.title: UK: INSTANT VIEW - UK August RPI data.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW - UK August RPI data.

text.p: Following is a selection of economists' reactions to UK data showing August retail prices (RPI) rising 0.5 percent m/m and 2.1 percent y/y, while RPIX was up 0.6 percent m/m and 2.8 percent y/y.
The consensus forecast was RPI +0.4 percent m/m and +2.1 y/y and RPIX +2.7 percent y/y.
"They are a little bit disappointing. They tend to rule out a rate cut or they certainly don't argue for a rate cut at the next Clarke-George meeting."

"I think for the rest of the year we can look forward to some good inflation figures. We'll probably find that the core measure of inflation does head towards the government target of 2.5 percent. But I don't think there's much scope for it go lower than that."

"The numbers were slightly above expectations. This seems to have come primarily from the rise in oil prices, which presumably will feed through again in September. It looks as if the improvement in inflation has stalled for now, but the medium term outlook will depend on what happens in the high street and whether retailers are able to raise their profit margins with the pickup in consumer spending."

"Underlying inflation failed to fall as many had expected. Seasonal food price rises from a year ago dropped out of the index in August, but they have been replaced by other things, such as higher clothing and footwear prices. RPIX looks amazingly flat, 2.8 percent for the past four straight months. Should nip any speculation of yet another rate cut in the bud."

"Slightly disappointing for the market. Big monthly rise in seasonal food prices and in petrol prices and the petrol price rise is likely to be sustained given what's happening to crude oil prices. It delays rather than completely eliminates the scope for inflation to fall in coming months...The encouraging thing is that the unwinding of the summer sales was not that aggressive, which would indicate that generally pricing pressures remain fairly competitive. I think interest rates are firmly on hold."
